purpose: Manufacturer-verified record for NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano 2, announced 2026-08-25 for low-power edge AI, local generative AI and robotics workloads.
notes: Only specifications explicitly disclosed by NVIDIA as of 2026-08-25 are recorded as verified facts.

NVIDIA has not yet published a public retail price, detailed memory-bandwidth figure, exact GPU/Tensor Core counts, module dimensions, storage configuration or full power-mode table for Jetson Orin Nano 2.
The 2x inference-performance and 40% lower-power claims are manufacturer comparisons against Jetson Orin Nano Super and are not normalized LLM token-generation benchmarks.

hardware.ai_compute_metric_note: NVIDIA states 78 trillion operations per second of AI compute; datatype/sparsity details were not specified in the launch release, so no datatype is inferred here.
hardware.memory_type: not yet publicly specified by NVIDIA
hardware.gpu_architecture: not yet publicly specified by NVIDIA in launch materials

power.notes: NVIDIA says the platform fits the same compact form factor and 40 W power envelope as the prior class, and that in 15 W mode it uses 40% less power to deliver the same performance as Jetson Orin Nano Super. Full supported power-mode table is not yet public.

performance_claims: NVIDIA claims approximately 2x the inference performance of Jetson Orin Nano Super.
NVIDIA claims 40% lower power at the same performance in 15 W mode versus Jetson Orin Nano Super.
hardware.quantization_compatibility: Expected to use NVIDIA Jetson/TensorRT memory-efficient inference paths and CUDA-compatible runtimes. Exact supported low-bit formats and runtime-version requirements for Jetson Orin Nano 2 should be recorded only after JetPack/TensorRT documentation for the device is published.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 8 GB memory makes this primarily a small-model edge platform. It should be treated as suitable for memory-efficient compact LLM/VLM workloads rather than large 20B-70B-class models. Actual fit depends on runtime, quantization, context length, KV cache and non-model memory overhead.
hardware.performance_per_watt: promising_vendor_claim_only; NVIDIA reports 2x predecessor inference performance and 40% lower power at equal performance in a 15 W mode, but model-specific tokens-per-watt data is not yet public
hardware.off_grid_suitability: very_high_potential; 15 W operating-mode evidence and a 40 W platform envelope make it a strong battery/solar candidate, but complete developer-kit wall-power measurements are still needed
hardware.physical_constraints: NVIDIA states the same compact form factor as Jetson Orin Nano Super; exact module/developer-kit dimensions for Nano 2 were not separately published in the announcement and are therefore not copied from the predecessor.
hardware.interfaces: not yet fully disclosed for Jetson Orin Nano 2; do not assume predecessor I/O without final module/developer-kit documentation

pricing.note: NVIDIA announced the module and developer kit for first-half 2027 availability but did not publish retail pricing in the launch release.

open_questions: GPU architecture/core counts and Tensor Core generation/count
